title: Extraction and qPCR of Environmental Surveillance samples for Salmonella Typhi
author: Jonathan Rigby

Thaw qPCR reagents and samples on ice and briefly spin down.
If stored in another microcentrifuge tube, pour the zirconia beads from a PowerBead tube included in the Qiagen PowerFaecal Pro kit into the tube and add 800 µL of CD1.

For this assay, six qPCR primer/probe targets are utilised. For S . Typhi, primers and probes targeting the staG and tviB genes and an intergenic region, currently named C6, are used. The control triplex targets ttr , a pan-salmonella gene; HF183, a Bacteroides dorei 16s human faecal indicator and the Sample Processing Control (SPC) from Eurogentec. Before ordering probes, please make sure you select the best fluorophores for the channels of your particular model of qPCR machine you will be using (see guidance note). steps.title: Prepare sample pellet or swab
steps.instruction: For a membrane‑filtration pellet, resuspend the pellet in 800 µL CD1 (from the first step of the DNA extraction protocol) and transfer the suspension to a PowerBead tube for homogenisation; for a Moore‑swab extraction, add 800 µL CD1 directly to the membrane strips already stored in PowerBead tubes.

steps.title: Add CD1 and SPC to PowerBead tube
steps.instruction: To the 800 µL CD1 already in the PowerBead tube add 1 µL validated Sample Processing Control (SPC) dilution from the Extraction and Inhibition Control kit.

substeps.instruction: Before first use of the SPC, prepare a 1/10 and a 1/100 dilution of the control DNA in pure water and keep on ice.

Evaluate the undiluted, 1/10 and 1/100 SPC dilutions in separate extractions by adding 1 µL of each control DNA to a reference sample before parallel extractions; after extraction and qPCR select the dilution that yields Ct values between 30 and 33.

steps.title: Homogenize sample
steps.instruction: Homogenise the PowerBead tube using a vortex adapter at maximum speed for up to 10 minutes (00:10:00).

steps.title: Centrifuge PowerBead tube
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the PowerBead tube at 15 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 minute.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant and add CD2
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a clean microcentrifuge tube, add 200 µL Solution CD2 and vortex for 5 seconds (00:00:05).

steps.title: Centrifuge and transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 15 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 minute and transfer up to 700 µL of the supernatant to a clean 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, avoiding the pellet.

steps.title: Add CD3 and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 600 µL Solution CD3 to the transferred supernatant and vortex for 5 seconds (00:00:05).

steps.title: Load lysate onto spin column
steps.instruction: Load 650 µL of the lysate onto an MB Spin Column and centrifuge at 15 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 minute. Discard the flow‑through and repeat loading (step above) until all lysate has passed through the column.

steps.title: Wash spin column with EA
steps.instruction: Place the spin column into a clean 2 mL collection tube, add 500 µL Solution EA, and centrifuge at 15 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 minute.

steps.title: Wash spin column with C5
steps.instruction: Discard the flow‑through, add 500 µL Solution C5 to the spin column and centrifuge at 15 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 minute.

steps.title: Final spin and dry column
steps.instruction: Discard the flow‑through, place the column in a clean 2 mL collection tube, centrifuge at 16 000 × g, room temperature, for 2 minutes, then transfer the column to a clean 1.5 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Elute DNA with C6
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL Solution C6 to the centre of the filter membrane, let sit for 1 minute, then centrifuge at 15 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 minute and discard the spin column.

steps.title: Store extracted DNA
steps.instruction: The eluate is now ready for qPCR or can be stored at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare primer and probe stocks
steps.instruction: Resuspend primers and probes in nuclease‑free water to make stock solutions of 20 µM for each primer and 5 µM for each probe.

steps.title: Prepare S Typhi qPCR master mix
steps.instruction: For each reaction prepare a 20 µL master mix containing: tviB_F 0.5 µL, tviB_R 0.5 µL, tviB_Pr 1 µL, staG_F 0.5 µL, staG_R 0.5 µL, staG_Pr 1 µL, C6_F 0.5 µL, C6_R 0.5 µL, C6_Pr 1 µL, 2× MasterMix with ROX 12.5 µL, nuclease‑free water 1.5 µL.

steps.title: Prepare control triplex master mix
steps.instruction: For each reaction prepare a 20 µL control master mix containing: ttr_F 0.5 µL, ttr_R 0.5 µL, ttr_Pr 1 µL, HF183_F 0.5 µL, HF183_R 0.5 µL, HF183_Pr 1 µL, 2× MasterMix with ROX 12.5 µL, 10× Control mix (Eurogentec) 2.5 µL, nuclease‑free water 1 µL.

steps.title: Aliquot master mixes to plate
steps.instruction: Dispense 20 µL of the appropriate master mix into each required well of a 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Add samples and controls
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of each DNA sample, positive control, extraction control, or 5 µL nuclease‑free water for negative‑control wells.

steps.title: Seal plate and spin
steps.instruction: Seal the plate with an adhesive plate seal, briefly spin the plate to collect liquids at the bottom of the wells and to remove bubbles.

steps.title: Run qPCR cycling program
steps.instruction: Load the plate into the real‑time PCR instrument and run the following program: 50 °C for 2 min (carry‑over prevention), 95 °C for 2 min (Takyon® activation), then 40 cycles of 95 °C for 15 s (denaturation), 60 °C for 30 s (annealing), 72 °C for 30 s (extension). Set data collection at the extension step if not automatic.

steps.title: Analyze Ct values
steps.instruction: After the run, assess normalised Ct values for each gene target in each sample and compare them to the cut‑off Ct values derived from the standard‑curve gBlock dilutions.

steps.title: Interpret results
steps.instruction: If all three S. Typhi targets (staG, tviB, C6) are positive, report the sample as S. Typhi positive. If only staG and tviB or only C6 are positive, report as suspected positive and proceed to amplicon sequencing. If ttr is positive and only one of staG or tviB is positive, repeat the negative target in a monoplex reaction. If all targets have Ct values above the cut‑off, examine the HF183 and SPC (spike‑in) controls: a negative or low‑Ct SPC indicates possible inhibition or extraction failure; a negative HF183 with a positive SPC suggests low or absent fecal contamination.

steps.title: Process extraction negative control
steps.instruction: Perform the extraction protocol on a tube containing only CD1 (no environmental sample) to serve as an extraction‑negative control.

steps.title: Process positive extraction control
steps.instruction: If a stock of positive DNA is not already available, extract DNA from a known S. Typhi isolate (Ty21a, ATCC/NCTC strain, or confirmed wild‑type isolate) to serve as a positive extraction control; this is distinct from the SPC added in step 2.

steps.title: QC screening of controls
steps.instruction: Screen the controls in both halves of the assay: (1) Positive control must amplify ttr, tviB, staG and C6; (2) Extraction NTC must show no amplification for any target except the SPC, which should have the expected Ct; (3) qPCR negative control must have no amplification for any target, including SPC. Deviations indicate contamination, inhibition, or assay failure.
